result.summary: The pedestrian environment is heavily impacted by a massive elevated rail structure that creates significant visual barriers and a fragmented walkway network. While a bike lane and sidewalk are present on the left, the right side is obstructed by large concrete pillars and debris, making for a hostile and poorly lit walking experience.

hazards.name: Pillar Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Large concrete pillars for the elevated rail structure block visibility between pedestrians and drivers, especially at the upcoming intersection.

hazards.name: Inadequate Walkway
hazards.description: The right side of the street lacks a clear, continuous sidewalk, with the space occupied by pillar bases and debris.

hazards.name: Debris and Litter
hazards.description: Significant accumulation of trash and debris on the right-side walkway area creates a tripping hazard and discourages pedestrian use.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to improve sightlines around the pillars and reduce the pedestrian crossing distance.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting under the elevated structure to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians during all hours.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Improvements
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, unobstructed sidewalk on the right side of the street to provide a safe path for pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features wide, continuous sidewalks situated beneath an elevated transit structure, which creates significant shadowing and a somewhat neglected atmosphere. While the walkways are spacious, they are impacted by accumulated debris and a lack of pedestrian-scale lighting or physical buffers from the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Debris
hazards.description: Accumulated trash and debris on the sidewalk create trip hazards and reduce the quality of the walking environment.

hazards.name: Poor Visibility
hazards.description: The overhead structure creates deep shadows that can obscure pedestrians from drivers and reduce personal security.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install lighting fixtures beneath the elevated structure to improve visibility and perceived safety for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Enhanced Maintenance
interventions.description: Establish a regular cleaning and maintenance program to keep the wide sidewalks clear of debris.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a large elevated transit structure, which provides overhead cover but creates significant visual obstructions with its support columns. While a wide sidewalk exists on one side, it is currently obstructed by debris and lacks clear, safe crossing points to the other side of the street.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Large black trash bags are placed directly on the walking path, forcing pedestrians to deviate.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Massive concrete and steel support columns for the elevated structure block sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the left side of the roadway.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalks at the nearest intersection to provide a designated and visible path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions (bulb-outs) at intersections to reduce crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond the columns.

result.summary: The image shows a wide concrete sidewalk along a commercial building with parallel on-street parking providing a buffer from traffic. The environment lacks marked crossings or active traffic calming, and the shuttered building frontage limits natural surveillance.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians who might attempt to cross the street mid-block.

hazards.name: Lack of natural surveillance
hazards.description: Shuttered windows and doors on the building frontage create a dead streetscape, reducing perceived safety through lack of eyes on the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the ends of the block or at a new mid-block crossing to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Add a marked crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a safe, designated place for pedestrians to cross.
